# About Abramson & Company LLC

## Identity

Abramson & Company LLC is a CPA firm headquartered at 278 Post Road East in Westport, Connecticut. Ray Abramson, CPA, founded the firm in its current form in 2005, and it operates under the tagline "We are passionate to meet your personal and business needs."

The team includes Ray Abramson, CPA (Principal), Kristen Rossi (Director of Operations), Lisa McEwan (Senior Accountant), Deborah Wamser, Chris Finelli, CPA, Rebecca Reineke, and Jason Smith Jr. (Accountants), Lindsay Brachle (Solution Specialist), and Beth Antunez (Admin). The firm describes its culture as team-oriented, with multiple team members familiar enough with each client to step in for one another, ensuring continuity of service.

The firm's tone is warm, reassuring, and client-focused, favoring plain-spoken, accessible language over technical jargon — reflecting a broader goal of reducing client stress and providing personalized support.

## Positioning & Differentiation

Abramson & Company positions itself as a CPA firm that treats every client like a neighbor, combining CPA-led expertise with genuine personal relationships and deep, specialized industry knowledge. This applies across real estate, professional services, retail, and nonprofit sectors, and extends to clients in Fairfield County, the tri-state area, the Bay Area, and nationwide.

The firm's stated differentiators include:

- Bundled services — bookkeeping, payroll, tax, and advisory — for a fixed monthly fee
- A secure online platform for real-time collaboration with clients
- Personalized tax strategies rather than one-size-fits-all preparation
- CPA-led expertise spanning bookkeeping, payroll, tax, and business advisory

The firm identifies a core client need: people have access to a lot of financial information but lack someone they can talk to and trust for personal guidance. Abramson positions its role as filling that gap — acting less like a transactional preparer and more like an ongoing financial partner that helps clients protect income, minimize taxes, and grow with confidence.

Services offered include Bookkeeping, Outsourced Accounting (bookkeeping, payroll, tax, and audit protection with account reconciliation and quarterly KPI review), Tax Plus (year-round personal tax support including deduction analysis, tax projections, options analysis, and expatriate tax), Payroll, Tax, Business Foundation Services (entity analysis, accounting system setup, retirement plan analysis), Audit Protection (IRS notice handling, state/federal representation, appeals and litigation support), Business Management Services (budgeting, revenue/expense/COGS analysis, tax planning), Financial Advice and Planning, and Advisory.

## Industries Served

### Real Estate

Abramson & Company provides specialized accounting expertise for real estate professionals, one of the firm's core niches alongside professional services, retail, and nonprofits.

### Professional Service Providers

The firm supports professional service businesses, including small doctor offices, independent physician groups, attorneys, marketing companies, and video production companies. Services are tailored to the accounting and advisory needs specific to these practice types.

### Retail

Abramson & Company offers expert accounting and advisory support for the retail industry, applying its broader bundled-service model — bookkeeping, payroll, tax, and advisory — to retail-specific needs.

### Equine

The firm serves clients with horse-related businesses and ownership, providing accounting support tailored to the equine industry. This is a quietly served niche rather than an actively promoted specialty.

### Influencers

Abramson & Company provides tax and accounting support for social media influencers. As with the equine niche, this is served quietly rather than featured as a primary marketing focus.

## Find the right form for your needs

Most accounting firms bury client paperwork in old email threads or a folder nobody can find twice. We built this page so that doesn't happen here. Starting with a new CPA firm usually means a stack of paperwork before anyone answers a real question. We keep the list short and specific:

- Engagement letter outlining scope, fees, and what to expect from bookkeeping, payroll, tax, or advisory work

Each of these arrives through your secure portal login once we've scheduled your first meeting, so you're never filling out the same information twice.

## Secure document upload and client portal access

Email was never built to carry a W-2 or a bank statement safely, so we don't use it for that. Every client gets a login to our secure online platform, where you can upload documents, review drafts, and message your CPA in real time instead of waiting for a callback.

The portal is also where engagement letters, signed authorizations, and finished tax returns land once they're ready. If you've misplaced your login, a quick call or email to your contact person gets it reset the same day. This is the same system our team uses internally, so what you upload shows up on our end instantly, not after someone forwards an attachment three times.

## Payroll and bookkeeping resource links

Clients running payroll or managing books across Connecticut, New York, and New Jersey need quick access to the agencies that set the rules. Here are the links we send most often:

- Connecticut Department of Labor, for state unemployment and new-hire reporting
- IRS, for federal withholding tables and EIN applications
- New York State Department of Labor, for tri-state employees on payroll
- New Jersey Department of Labor and Workforce Development, for NJ-based staff
- Connecticut Department of Revenue Services, for state tax registration and filing

If a form on one of these sites doesn't match your situation, that's usually a sign it's time to loop in your bookkeeping or payroll contact here before you file anything.

### Refund tracker
URL: /resources/refund-tracker

## Check your refund status in minutes

You don't need to dig through government websites to find out where your money is. For your federal refund, the IRS **Where's My Refund** tool at [irs.gov/refunds](https://www.irs.gov/refunds) gives you a status update within 24 hours of e-filing (or about four weeks after mailing a paper return). For your Connecticut state refund, the Department of Revenue Services runs its tracker through **myconneCT** at [portal.ct.gov/drs](https://portal.ct.gov/drs/individuals/individual-tax-page/status-of-refund). Both tools are free, and both update once a day, usually overnight, so checking more than once every 24 hours won't get you a different answer.

If you filed with Abramson & Company, we can also pull up your filing confirmation and refund amount on request, no login required on your end.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: taxpayer-checking-refund-status.jpg | alt: "Person checking tax refund status on laptop at home desk" | query: "person checking laptop tax documents" -->
## What to have ready before you check

Both the IRS and Connecticut systems will reject your lookup if any detail is slightly off. Have these on hand before you click through:

- Your Social Security number or ITIN
- Your exact filing status (single, married filing jointly, head of household, etc.)
- The exact refund amount shown on your return, down to the dollar
- For CT specifically, the tax year you're checking
- A few extra minutes, since typing errors are the most common reason people see an error message

If you filed jointly, use the SSN listed first on the return. That trips up more people than anything else.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: reviewing-tax-refund-timeline.jpg | alt: "Accountant reviewing a tax return timeline with a client" | query: "accountant client reviewing paperwork office" -->
## Typical refund timelines

Timing depends on how you filed and how you're getting paid. E-filed federal returns with direct deposit typically arrive within 21 days. Paper federal returns run six to eight weeks, sometimes longer during peak season. Connecticut refunds generally take longer than federal ones: the DRS estimates 10 to 12 weeks for a processed return, and paper CT returns can stretch past that.

A few things speed things up: filing early, e-filing instead of mailing, and choosing direct deposit over a paper check. A few things slow things down: filing close to the April deadline, claiming certain credits that trigger extra review, or mailing an amended return, which the IRS says can take up to 16 weeks to process.

None of these timelines are promises. They're patterns we see year after year with clients across Westport, Fairfield County, and the tri-state area.

## Common reasons your refund is delayed

A delay usually isn't a red flag. It's often one of these:

A math error or a mismatched Social Security number triggers a manual review, which adds time but rarely changes the outcome. Identity verification requests, where the IRS asks you to confirm you filed the return, are increasingly common and simply require a response, not a correction. Amended returns take longer by design, since they're reviewed by hand rather than run through automated processing. And if you owe back taxes, child support, or certain federal debts, the Treasury Offset Program can reduce or redirect your refund before it reaches you, something you'd typically be notified about separately.

If your status shows "still processing" for more than 21 days past your e-file date, that's the point worth paying attention to, not panicking over.

## When to reach out to our team

Checking a portal once a day is reasonable. Refreshing it five times before lunch isn't going to change the outcome, and it's a good sign it's time to call someone who can actually look into it.

Reach out to us if your refund is more than 21 days late for an e-filed federal return, more than 12 weeks late for a Connecticut return, if you've received an identity verification letter and aren't sure how to respond, or if your refund amount doesn't match what we filed. Because our team works together on every client file, whoever picks up the phone can pull up your return and give you a straight answer, not a generic script.

<!-- block: cta-banner | variant: image-bg | image: cpa-consultation-westport-ct.jpg | alt: "CPA meeting with a client at a desk in a Westport office" | query: "cpa meeting client office consultation" -->
## Get personalized help with your tax return

A refund tracker can tell you where your money is. It can't tell you why your withholding was off, whether you're missing a credit, or how to plan next year so the refund is bigger, or smaller, on purpose. That's the conversation we have with clients throughout Westport, Fairfield County, and the tri-state area, plus a growing number in California's Bay Area, every tax season.

If you have questions about a delayed refund, a notice you received, or how to set up next year's return so there are fewer surprises, [schedule a consultation](/contact) with Abramson & Company. We'll look at the actual return, not just the status bar.

## Industries we serve

### Real estate accounting
URL: /industries/real-estate

<!-- block: intro-text | variant: centered -->
## Accounting built for real estate professionals

Agents chasing commissions, brokers running teams, investors juggling five or six properties, developers mid-construction, property managers reconciling rent rolls: real estate income never looks the same from one client to the next. Most of what's online about real estate taxes is generic. It tells you depreciation exists but not how to apply it to your triplex in Westport or your flip in New Canaan.

What real estate professionals in Fairfield County actually need is someone who picks up the phone, knows the deal structure, and has already thought through the tax angle before the closing date arrives. Abramson & Company has worked with real estate clients across Westport, CT, Fairfield County, and the tri-state area since 2005, and we build the financial side of your business around how you actually earn money, not a template.

<!-- block: service-cards | variant: 3-col -->
## Services tailored to property income and transactions

Property income rarely fits into one bucket. Rental cash flow, commission checks, 1031 proceeds, and construction draws each carry different tax treatment and different bookkeeping needs. Here's how our services line up against the real estate specifics that actually matter.

### Bookkeeping
icon: Calculator

We track rent rolls, security deposits, commission splits, and property-level expenses so every unit or listing has its own clean set of books, not one blended ledger that hides what's actually profitable.

### Outsourced Accounting
icon: Briefcase

For investors and developers managing multiple entities, we handle the full accounting function, month-end close, financial statements, and reconciliations across each LLC, so you get one clear picture instead of five disconnected spreadsheets.

### Tax Plus
icon: FileCheck

Ongoing tax support built around real estate timing: 1031 exchange deadlines, cost segregation studies, and depreciation schedules reviewed before decisions get made, not after the return is filed.

### Payroll
icon: Users

Property management teams and brokerages with support staff get payroll that handles commission-based pay structures and multi-state employees without the filing headaches.

### Tax
icon: Coins

Personal and business returns prepared with attention to passive activity rules, rental loss limitations, and the entity structure behind each property you hold.

### Business Foundation Services
icon: Building2

Setting up a new LLC for an acquisition or restructuring how you hold multiple properties? We help you choose an entity structure that fits your tax picture and your exit plan.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: real-estate-tax-planning.jpg | alt: "Accountant and real estate investor reviewing property tax documents together" | query: "real estate investor meeting accountant" -->
## Tax strategies for investors, agents, and property owners

Depreciation sounds simple until you're weighing a cost segregation study against the cost of the study itself, or deciding whether a rental loss is deductible this year under the passive activity rules. Agents face a different problem: commission income that swings wildly month to month, with quarterly estimates due whether the deal closed or not.

We build tax strategy around your calendar, not April's. That means reviewing depreciation schedules and entity structure before year-end, flagging when a cost segregation study makes sense on a new acquisition, and setting quarterly estimates that reflect what you're actually earning rather than last year's numbers. For clients holding several properties, we look at the portfolio as a whole so losses on one property aren't quietly wasted while another owes tax it didn't need to.

The goal is simple: fewer surprises at filing time, and a strategy you understood months before it mattered.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: real-estate-platform-dashboard.jpg | alt: "Real estate professional checking financial dashboard on laptop and phone" | query: "person using laptop financial dashboard" -->
## Real-time financial visibility through our secure platform

A lender wants updated financials before Friday. A partner asks how a property performed last quarter. A deal is closing and you need current numbers, not last month's. Real estate moves fast, and waiting on a callback isn't realistic when you're managing several properties or transactions at once.

Our secure online platform gives you real-time access to your books, so you can pull current numbers for a lender request, a partner update, or a due diligence packet without waiting on us to send a file.

- See income and expenses by property, updated as transactions are entered
- Share financials securely with lenders, partners, or attorneys when a deal needs proof of numbers
- Message your accounting team directly inside the platform instead of chasing an email thread
- Pull reports on demand for a refinance, sale, or year-end review

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-left | image: local-cpa-team-real-estate.jpg | alt: "CPA team members discussing a client's real estate portfolio in office" | query: "accounting team meeting office" -->
## A team that knows your properties and your goals

When you call with a question about your Bridgeport rental or a 1031 deadline coming up next week, you shouldn't have to explain your whole portfolio from scratch because the one person who knew it is out of the office. We run a team-oriented culture where more than one staff member knows your properties, your entity structure, and what you're working toward, so someone is always ready to help.

Abramson & Company has served real estate professionals from our Westport, CT office since 2005, with clients throughout Fairfield County and the tri-state area of Connecticut, New York, and New Jersey. We also work with clients in California, including the Bay Area, using the same secure platform and the same direct access to your team, regardless of time zone.

<!-- block: cta-banner | variant: image-bg | image: real-estate-agent-consultation.jpg | alt: "Real estate agent shaking hands after a financial consultation meeting" | query: "real estate agent handshake meeting" -->

Whether you're closing your first rental purchase or managing a portfolio across three states, the numbers behind it deserve more than a generic template. Our bundled services come with a fixed monthly fee, so you know your cost upfront and can add bookkeeping, tax, payroll, and advisory support as your portfolio grows, without a surprise invoice.

## Accounting built for consultants, agencies, and firms

<!-- block: intro-text | variant: centered -->
Professional service firms run on billable hours, but the accounting behind them rarely fits into neat boxes. One month brings a wave of retainer income, the next brings a slow trickle while you wait on invoices. Entity structure decisions, whether you're an LLC, S-corp, or partnership, change your tax picture every year you grow. A generic bookkeeper who handles restaurants and retail shops on the side isn't going to catch the nuances of a consulting practice or a boutique law firm.

Abramson & Company is a CPA firm in Westport, CT that works specifically with consultants, agencies, and professional service providers across Fairfield County and the tri-state area. We've built our process around irregular cash flow, project-based revenue, and the entity questions that come with adding partners or scaling a team. This is not a once-a-year filing relationship. It's ongoing support from people who already understand how your business makes money.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: consultant-reviewing-financials.jpg | alt: "Professional service provider reviewing financial reports with a CPA" | query: "consultant meeting accountant office" -->
## Bookkeeping and outsourced accounting for busy practices

Most professional service providers didn't start their firm to spend evenings reconciling bank feeds. Our [bookkeeping](/services/bookkeeping) and [outsourced accounting](/services/outsourced-accounting) services combine into a single bundled package for one fixed monthly fee, so there's no surprise invoice when your books get more complicated.

You get access to a secure online platform where you and our team see the same numbers in real time, no waiting for a monthly PDF or a callback. If you're managing project-based billing across multiple clients, that visibility matters: you can check margins on a contract or confirm cash on hand before making a hiring decision, without waiting for us to send a report.

This is the kind of support a growing consulting firm or agency actually uses, not a service that sits unopened in an inbox once a quarter.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-left | image: tax-planning-professional-firm.jpg | alt: "CPA discussing tax strategy documents with a professional services client" | query: "tax planning meeting office documents" -->
## Tax planning and preparation for service-based businesses

Service-based businesses tend to get hit hardest by once-a-year tax prep, because so much of what determines your bill (entity structure, retirement contributions, quarterly estimates, how you pay yourself) has to be decided before December 31, not after. Our [Tax](/services/tax) and Tax Plus services are built around planning throughout the year, not just filing in April.

For consultants and professional firms, that often means reviewing your entity election as revenue grows, timing income and expenses around project cycles, and coordinating owner compensation with retirement contributions. We also handle [personal income tax](/services/personal-income-tax) alongside your business return, since for most owners the two are inseparable.

The goal is a strategy you understand and revisit with us, not a form that shows up once a year with a number attached.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: payroll-team-professional-services.jpg | alt: "Small professional services team reviewing payroll and staffing documents" | query: "small business team payroll paperwork" -->
## Payroll and business foundation support as you grow

Adding your first employee, or your fifth, changes the administrative load on a professional service firm fast. Our [payroll](/services/payroll) service handles the filings, deposits, and compliance work so you're not learning state withholding rules between client calls. For firms bringing on 1099 contractors, subcontracted specialists, or part-time staff, we set up the systems correctly the first time.

[Business Foundation Services](/services/business-foundation-services/) cover the groundwork many growing firms skip: entity setup, accounting system structure, and the internal controls that keep books clean as headcount rises.

- Payroll processing, tax filings, and new-hire compliance
- Contractor payments and 1099 tracking
- Entity structure and accounting system setup for scaling firms
- Ongoing support as staffing needs shift

This is the administrative work that quietly eats a founder's week. We take it off your plate so client work stays the priority.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: cpa-advisory-meeting-westport.jpg | alt: "CPA advisor and business owner reviewing financial plan together" | query: "financial advisor client consultation office" -->
## Audit protection and financial advice when it matters

An IRS notice or a client audit request can stall a professional service firm for weeks if you're not prepared. Our [Audit Protection](/services/audit-protection) service gives you a direct line to someone who already knows your books, so you're not starting from scratch explaining your business to a stranger under deadline pressure.

Beyond compliance, growth decisions (bringing on a partner, opening a second office, evaluating a retirement plan) deserve more than a guess. We work alongside clients on [business management](/services/business-management-services) and [retirement plan analysis](/services/retirement-plan-analysis) questions as they come up, not just at tax time.

Having someone to call before you make a decision, not just after, is the difference between reacting to problems and planning around them.

### Retail accounting
URL: /industries/retail

<!-- block: intro-text | variant: centered -->
## Accounting support made for retail businesses

Retail runs on thin margins and constant movement. Cash in the register at open, card swipes all day, online orders overnight, and a stockroom that never quite matches what the shelves show. Add seasonal swings around the holidays and back-to-school, and closing the books each month can feel like chasing a moving target.

Abramson & Company has worked with retail owners across Westport and Fairfield County since 2005, so we know where the numbers usually go sideways: POS reconciliation, inventory valuation, and sales tax across multiple states if you sell online. CPA-led support means every recommendation, from cash flow timing to tax strategy, comes from someone who has actually reviewed your numbers, not a call center reading from a script.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: retail-pos-reconciliation.jpg | alt: "Retail store owner reviewing point-of-sale reports with accountant" | query: "retail store owner checking receipts" -->
## Bookkeeping and POS reconciliation for retail stores

Daily sales run through more channels than most retail owners have time to track: cash drawers, credit card terminals, e-commerce platforms, and sometimes a second or third store location. Our [bookkeeping](/services/bookkeeping) service reconciles POS reports against bank deposits and merchant statements every week, not just at month-end, so discrepancies get caught while you still remember what happened that Tuesday afternoon.

Bookkeeping integrates with the POS and payment systems you already run, whether that's Square, Shopify, Clover, or a legacy system tied to your inventory management. You get a clean, current set of books through Abramson's secure online platform, where you can see reconciled sales, cost of goods, and margins without waiting for a phone call back. That means faster answers on which items are actually profitable and less time spent second-guessing your own numbers.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: retail-payroll-seasonal-staff.jpg | alt: "Retail employee working a shift at store checkout counter" | query: "retail employee working checkout counter" -->
## Payroll built for retail schedules and seasonal staffing

Retail payroll rarely looks like a typical 9-to-5 spreadsheet. Hourly shifts change week to week, holiday hiring spikes headcount for six weeks and then drops it back down, and an owner might run [payroll](/services/payroll) across two or three store locations with different state tax rules. Getting it wrong means back pay corrections, penalty notices, or a seasonal hire who never got the right withholding.

- Hourly and shift-based payroll processed on the schedule your stores actually run
- Seasonal hires onboarded and offboarded without compliance gaps
- Multi-location payroll handled under one system, even across CT, NY, and NJ
- Tip reporting and minimum wage compliance built into every pay run
- Direct integration with your bookkeeping, so labor costs show up in your margins automatically

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-left | image: retail-tax-planning-meeting.jpg | alt: "Accountant reviewing tax documents with retail store owner" | query: "accountant discussing taxes retail owner" -->
## Tax planning and preparation for retail businesses

Inventory valuation method, sales tax nexus across states, and depreciation on store fixtures each shape your retail tax bill differently than a typical service business. A change in how you value inventory, LIFO versus FIFO for example, can move taxable income by a meaningful amount, and most retail owners never get advice on it until year-end, when there's nothing left to plan.

Abramson builds a personalized [tax](/services/tax) strategy around your sales cycle: quarterly check-ins before your busy season, not a single meeting in March. Retail deductions around store buildout, equipment, and shrinkage get identified while there's still time to act on them. [Audit protection](/services/audit-protection) is built into the relationship too, so if a sales tax audit or an IRS inquiry lands on your desk, you're not facing it without the CPA who prepared the return in the first place.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: retail-growth-financial-review.jpg | alt: "Retail owner reviewing financial dashboard on laptop in store" | query: "retail owner laptop store dashboard" -->
## Financial insight to guide retail growth decisions

Deciding whether to open a second location, buy inventory ahead of a price increase, or add three more part-time staff for the holidays requires numbers you can trust today, not a report from six weeks ago. [Outsourced accounting](/services/outsourced-accounting) keeps your financials current and reviewed by a CPA, so the cash flow projection you're looking at reflects this month's reality.

Abramson's secure online platform gives you real-time access to sales trends, margin by category, and cash position, along with direct messaging to your accounting team when a number doesn't look right. [Business management services](/services/business-management-services) layer on top for owners weighing a lease renewal, a new POS system, or a hiring decision, turning bookkeeping data into an actual growth plan instead of a spreadsheet nobody opens.

### Video Production
URL: /industries/video-production

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: video-production-accounting-intro.jpg | alt: "Video production crew reviewing budget documents on set" | query: "video production crew reviewing paperwork" -->
## Accounting built around how video production companies work

Video production income rarely lands the same way twice. One month you're invoicing a client for a six-figure commercial shoot; the next you're waiting forty-five days on a production payment while covering gear rentals, freelance editors, and a small crew of contractors. Generic bookkeeping software wasn't built for that rhythm, and neither was the accountant down the street.

Abramson & Company works with production companies across Westport, CT and Fairfield County who need a CPA firm that already understands project-based revenue, equipment-heavy budgets, and a workforce that shifts from job to job. Our bookkeeping, payroll, and tax services are built around that reality instead of asking you to fit a standard small-business template. That means fewer surprises at tax time and a clearer read on cash flow between projects.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: video-production-bookkeeping-team.jpg | alt: "Accountant and production manager reviewing invoices on a laptop" | query: "accountant reviewing invoices laptop office" -->
## Bookkeeping and outsourced accounting for production budgets and client billing

Production budgets rarely stay still. A single project might involve a client retainer, rental deposits, freelancer invoices, and reimbursable expenses, all moving at different speeds. Our [bookkeeping](/services/bookkeeping) and [outsourced accounting](/services/outsourced-accounting) services keep those pieces reconciled in one place, on a secure online platform where you see real-time numbers instead of waiting for a monthly PDF.

Bundled under one fixed monthly fee, this service covers:

- Project-by-project budget tracking so you know margin on each shoot, not just overall revenue
- Client invoicing and collections support to keep cash flow steady between productions
- Vendor and equipment rental payment tracking, so nothing slips through the cracks
- Monthly reconciliation and reporting your team can review without decoding spreadsheets

The goal is straightforward: your creative team spends time on production, not chasing receipts.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-left | image: video-production-crew-payroll.jpg | alt: "Production crew members on set during a filming setup" | query: "film crew working on set" -->
## Payroll for crews, freelancers, and contractors

A single shoot day might involve a full-time production manager on payroll, three freelance camera operators paid 1099, and a per-project gaffer working under a union agreement. Classifying each person correctly, and paying them on time, is where a lot of production companies get into trouble with the IRS or state labor departments.

Abramson & Company's [payroll](/services/payroll) service handles W-2 staff, 1099 contractor payments, and per-project crew in one system, so you're not juggling three separate processes for three types of workers. We track worker classification, filing deadlines, and year-end 1099 and W-2 issuance, and flag misclassification risk before it becomes a problem. Crews get paid accurately and on schedule, and you get a payroll record that holds up if a filing ever gets questioned.

<!-- block: feature-grid | variant: 3-col -->
## Tax planning and deductions specific to video and media production

Production companies carry deductions most small businesses never touch, and miss others because nobody flagged them. [Personalized tax strategy](/services/tax) for a media business looks different than for a retail shop, and that's where planning ahead of the return matters more than the return itself.

### Equipment depreciation
icon: Wallet

Cameras, lenses, lighting rigs, and edit bay hardware depreciate on a schedule that rewards planning your purchases, not just recording them after the fact. We help you time equipment buys against Section 179 and bonus depreciation rules so a big gear purchase works for your tax bill instead of against it.

### Home studio and office deductions
icon: Home

Many production owners run pre-production, editing, or client meetings from a home office or converted studio space. We calculate the deduction correctly, square footage, utilities, and depreciation included, so you claim what you're entitled to without raising a flag.

### Production-related expense deductions
icon: FileText

Location fees, travel to shoots, insurance, and post-production software subscriptions all carry deduction rules specific to project-based creative work. We track these against your bookkeeping records so nothing gets missed at filing time.

### Connecticut digital media tax credit guidance
icon: Award

Connecticut offers a sliding-scale tax credit for qualified digital media and motion picture production expenses. We help determine whether your production activity and spending qualify, and walk through the documentation the state requires.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: video-production-company-growth-meeting.jpg | alt: "Small business owner and accountant discussing growth plans at a desk" | query: "business owner accountant discussing growth plans" -->
## Business advisory support as your production company grows

Plenty of production companies start as one person with a camera and a laptop, then grow into an agency with a full crew, a studio lease, and multiple concurrent projects. Each stage raises a different question: stay a sole proprietor or move to an S-corp? Set up a formal budget process before hiring? How much to set aside for slow months?

[Business Foundation Services](/services/business-foundation-services/) help you choose the right entity structure and set up financial systems that scale with you, from a freelance operation to a full production house. [Business Management Services](/services/business-management-services) cover the longer view: profit distribution, retirement planning, and the financial decisions that come with owning a growing creative business.

## Bookkeeping support that gives you peace of mind

Falling behind on your books creates a quiet kind of stress. You know it's there even when you're not looking at it. For small business owners in Westport and across Fairfield County, that unease usually comes from not knowing where the numbers actually stand.

Abramson & Company built its bookkeeping service around a simple idea: you should never have to guess. Every transaction gets categorized, every account gets reconciled, and every report reaches you before you have to ask for it. Founded in 2005, our firm treats bookkeeping as the foundation everything else rests on, from tax planning to the advice you need to grow. When the books are clean, the rest of the picture gets a lot easier to see.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: bookkeeper-reviewing-documents.jpg | alt: "Bookkeeper reviewing financial documents and receipts at a desk" | query: "bookkeeper reviewing financial documents desk" -->
## What our bookkeeping services include

Bookkeeping done right is more than data entry. Our team categorizes every transaction, reconciles bank and credit card accounts monthly, and delivers financial statements you can actually read and use. Here's what's included:

- Transaction categorization and coding, done consistently every month
- Bank and credit card reconciliations to catch errors before they compound
- Monthly profit and loss statements and balance sheets
- Accounts payable and receivable tracking
- Custom reporting built around the metrics that matter to your business
- Direct coordination with your CPA on tax questions as they come up

Bookkeeping is also the entry point into two of our other services. Clients who want a fully outsourced finance function often move into [Outsourced Accounting](/services/outsourced-accounting), where we handle month-end close and management reporting. Those who want tax strategy woven into their monthly numbers add [Tax Plus](/services/tax), so nothing gets discovered for the first time in April.

## One fixed monthly fee, no surprises

Hourly billing punishes you for asking questions. Call your bookkeeper twice in a week and you might see it reflected on the invoice. We don't work that way.

Every bookkeeping client pays one fixed monthly fee that bundles bookkeeping with the related services you need, whether that's payroll, tax prep, or advisory support. You know the number before the month starts, and it doesn't move because you emailed us three times instead of one.

That predictability matters most when cash flow is already tight. Fixed-fee bundling lets you budget for accounting the way you budget for rent or payroll, without worrying that a busy month turns into a surprise bill.

## Real-time access through our secure client platform

Not knowing where your numbers stand between meetings is its own kind of stress. Our secure online platform gives you real-time access to your books, so you can check your cash position at 9pm on a Tuesday without waiting for a callback.

You'll see reconciled transactions, current financial statements, and shared documents in one place. If a question comes up, you can flag it directly in the platform instead of digging through an email thread from three weeks ago.

It's the same information we're looking at, updated on the same schedule we update it, so you're never working from an outdated picture of your own business.

## Bookkeeping tailored to your industry

Every industry keeps its books a little differently. A property manager's chart of accounts doesn't look like a boutique's, and a veterinary practice tracks costs a retail shop never has to think about. We've built bookkeeping workflows around the niches we know best, plus a few industries most local firms overlook.

<!-- block: industry-cards | variant: 3-col -->
### Real Estate
icon: Home

Property managers and investors need bookkeeping that tracks income and expenses by property, not just by month. We reconcile security deposits, CAM charges, and escrow so reports match what your lender expects to see. See our [real estate accounting work](/industries/real-estate).

### Professional Service Providers
icon: Briefcase

Law firms, consultants, and agencies bill by project or retainer, and your books should reflect that. We track work-in-progress and unbilled time so revenue recognition lines up with cash actually collected. Learn more about our [professional service provider support](/industries/professional-service-providers).

### Retail
icon: Building2

Inventory, point-of-sale integration, and sales tax across jurisdictions complicate retail books fast. We reconcile daily sales data against deposits so shrinkage and errors surface quickly. Explore our [retail bookkeeping approach](/industries/retail).

### Equine
icon: HeartPulse

Boarding fees, veterinary costs, and seasonal cash flow make equine businesses harder to track than most bookkeepers realize. We've built the categories that fit how horse operations actually run.

### Influencers
icon: Sparkles

Brand deals, affiliate income, and gifted product all count as revenue, and the IRS expects it reported correctly. We track irregular income streams so tax season doesn't turn into a scramble.

### Construction
icon: Hammer

Job costing, retainage, and progress billing require bookkeeping that goes deeper than a standard general ledger. We track costs by job so you know which projects actually make money.

### Healthcare
icon: Stethoscope

Insurance reimbursements, payer mix, and practice overhead move on their own timeline. We reconcile receivables against what payers actually remit, not just what was billed.

## How our fixed monthly fee model simplifies tax planning

Most firms bill by the form, the hour, or the phone call, which makes tax costs unpredictable and turns every question into a line item.

- One flat monthly fee bundles tax planning, preparation, bookkeeping, payroll, and advisory support, so there's no surprise invoice for asking a question in October.
- A secure online platform lets you upload documents, message your CPA, and review your return in real time, from a phone, a laptop, or a client sitting in California at 9 a.m. Pacific.
- Personalized tax strategies get built around your actual return, not a generic checklist, because planning happens throughout the year instead of during a two-week rush in April.

This model exists because clients told Abramson & Company the same thing for years: they wanted to know what tax help would cost before they called, not after. ## Choosing the right entity structure for your goals

LLC or S-corp isn't a question with one right answer. A retail shop owner in Westport and a real estate investor building a portfolio in Fairfield County often land in different structures even when their revenue numbers look similar.

We walk through the tax consequences of each option with you, not at you. That means modeling out self-employment tax exposure, distribution rules, and filing obligations before you file anything, so the structure you choose supports where the business is actually headed instead of where a template assumed it would go.

### Audit protection
URL: /services/audit-protection

<!-- block: intro-text | variant: centered -->
## Fear no audit with a CPA-led defense team

An IRS notice in the mailbox can ruin a week. Most business owners open it, feel their stomach drop, and have no idea what happens next. That's the moment Abramson & Company steps in.

We respond to the IRS and Connecticut Department of Revenue Services directly on your behalf, so you're not the one on the phone trying to decode agency language. Since founding the firm in 2005, Ray Abramson has built a team that treats audit defense as a core discipline, not an afterthought bolted onto tax prep. You get a CPA between you and the auditor, handling correspondence, deadlines, and documentation while you keep running your business. That's the whole point of audit protection: fewer sleepless nights, one clear point of contact, and someone in your corner who already knows your file.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: audit-notice-review.jpg | alt: "CPA reviewing an IRS audit notice with a client at a desk" | query: "accountant reviewing tax documents client" -->
## What our audit protection covers

Audit protection through Abramson & Company isn't a single phone call. It's a defined scope of work that stays active for as long as an inquiry runs, covering:

- Direct response to IRS notices and letters, including CP2000s, underreporter notices, and audit selection letters
- Handling of Connecticut Department of Revenue Services notices and other state tax authority correspondence
- Representation at the examination and appeals level, so you're not sitting across the table alone
- Support through litigation-track matters when a case escalates beyond standard appeals
- Ongoing communication with the assigned agent or auditor, tracked and documented so nothing falls through a gap
- Coordination with your bookkeeping and tax records already on file with our team, cutting down the scramble to find documentation

Every response goes out under CPA review before it reaches the IRS or state. You'll know what's been sent, when, and why.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: westport-office-team.jpg | alt: "Accounting team collaborating in a Westport Connecticut office" | query: "accounting team office meeting Connecticut" -->
## Why Westport and Fairfield County businesses choose us

Local knowledge matters when a state notice arrives, and geography still shapes half the questions we field. We work with individuals and small-to-midsize businesses across Westport, Fairfield County, and the wider tri-state area of Connecticut, New York, and New Jersey, plus a growing group of clients in California's Bay Area who found us through referral.

The firm runs on a team-oriented model: more than one person on staff knows your file well enough to step in if your usual contact is out. That matters most during an audit, when a state deadline doesn't wait for someone's vacation. You're not tied to a single name on a business card. You're tied to a firm that already has your history, your numbers, and your context on hand.

<!-- block: industry-cards | variant: 3-col -->
## Audit protection tailored to your industry

Auditors look for different red flags depending on what you do. Generic advice misses the details that actually trigger a notice, so our approach shifts by industry.

### Real Estate
icon: Home

Depreciation schedules, 1031 exchanges, and passive activity loss rules draw scrutiny in real estate audits. We prepare documentation on entity structure and property transactions before an inquiry ever arrives.

### Professional Service Providers
icon: Briefcase

Attorneys, consultants, and other service providers face questions about business use of home offices, owner compensation, and deductible expenses. We keep the paper trail organized so those answers are ready.

### Retail
icon: Building2

Inventory valuation, cash transactions, and sales tax reconciliation are common audit triggers for retail businesses. We tie your point-of-sale and bookkeeping records together so the numbers match every filing.

### Equine
icon: HeartPulse

Hobby-loss rules hit equine operations harder than almost any other niche, since the IRS routinely questions whether a horse business is run for profit. We document the operational and financial case that it is.

### Influencers
icon: Sparkles

Gifted products, brand deals, and mixed personal-business expenses create audit exposure unique to influencer income. We help classify income correctly from the start, so an audit finds consistency instead of confusion.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-left | image: secure-client-portal.jpg | alt: "Business owner reviewing financial reports on a secure online client portal" | query: "business owner laptop financial dashboard" -->
## How audit protection fits into your fixed monthly plan

Audit protection isn't sold as a surprise add-on when a notice shows up. It's built into the bundled, fixed-monthly-fee model that covers bookkeeping, payroll, tax, and advisory work under one plan. You know the cost before anything happens, not after.

Everything runs through the same secure online platform where you already track invoices, payroll runs, and tax filings. When a notice comes in, the team pulling your defense together is looking at the same live numbers you are, in real time, instead of requesting documents from scratch. That continuity is the difference between a defense built on guesswork and one built on records that were accurate the day they were filed.

<!-- block: process-steps | variant: vertical -->
## What to expect if you receive an audit notice

### Call us before you respond to anything

Don't sign, mail, or email anything back to the IRS or state on your own. Call your Abramson & Company contact first, ideally within 24 to 48 hours of opening the notice.

### Send us the notice

Upload the letter through the secure client portal or forward it directly. We confirm receipt and flag the response deadline immediately so nothing lapses.

### We review and respond

A CPA on your account reviews the notice against your existing records, drafts the response, and handles direct correspondence with the agency on your behalf.

### We keep you posted

You get a plain-language update at each stage, whether the matter closes in one letter or moves toward an appeals-level review.

Most people call us after the notice arrives. The smarter move is calling before one does. Since 2005, Abramson & Company has built audit defense into the everyday work of running a business in Westport, Fairfield County, and beyond, so it's already there when you need it.

### Entity type analysis
URL: /services/entity-type-analysis

<!-- block: intro-text | variant: centered -->
## Choosing the right structure shapes your tax and liability future

Every business decision starts with a structure. LLC, S-corp, C-corp, partnership, or sole proprietorship: each carries its own tax treatment, liability exposure, and paperwork burden. Pick wrong, and you could pay more in self-employment tax than necessary, or leave personal assets exposed to business debt. Pick right, and the structure quietly supports growth for years without you thinking about it again.

For business owners in Westport and across Fairfield County, entity type analysis is one of the first services under Abramson & Company's [Business Foundation Services](/services/business-foundation-services/). It's a deliberate review of income projections, liability risk, and long-term plans, conducted by a CPA who asks the right questions before recommending a direction. New ventures and established companies both need this review: the tax code doesn't stay still, and neither should your entity choice.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: business-owner-entity-review.jpg | alt: "Small business owner reviewing entity structure paperwork with an advisor" | query: "small business owner meeting advisor documents" -->
## Who benefits most from a professional entity review

New business owners face this decision on day one, often without knowing how much it matters. A [real estate](/industries/real-estate) investor forming an LLC for a rental property, a [professional service provider](/industries/professional-service-providers) setting up a consulting practice, or a [retail](/industries/retail) owner opening a second location each face a different calculation. Guess wrong, and unwinding the paperwork later costs more than getting it right the first time.

Established businesses need this review too. An equine business scaling from hobby to full operation, an influencer whose income has outgrown a sole proprietorship, or a retail partnership bringing on new owners all reach a point where the original structure no longer fits. Restructuring isn't a sign something went wrong. It's what growth looks like on paper.

<!-- block: process-steps | variant: vertical -->
## How our CPA-led process works

### Understanding your goals
The process starts with a conversation about where the business is headed: revenue targets, hiring plans, potential investors, and how you eventually want to exit. This context shapes everything that follows, more than any generic checklist could.

### Reviewing income and liability exposure
A CPA walks through projected income, self-employment tax exposure, and the personal liability risk tied to your current or planned structure. Real numbers replace guesswork at this stage.

### Weighing the options
LLC, S-corp, C-corp, partnership, or sole proprietorship: each option gets compared against your actual projections, not textbook assumptions. Some structures that look appealing on paper create tax problems once your specific numbers are run through them.

### Recommending a structure in plain language
You get a clear recommendation with the reasoning behind it, explained without jargon, so the decision makes sense before anything gets filed. Questions get answered on the spot, not weeks later in a follow-up email.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: online-platform-collaboration.jpg | alt: "Business owner and CPA reviewing financial dashboard on a laptop together" | query: "business owner accountant laptop collaboration" -->
## Support that continues after you choose a structure

Entity selection isn't a form filed and forgotten. Once a structure is set, it connects directly to how your books are kept, how payroll runs, and how your tax return gets filed each year. Abramson & Company bundles these services under one fixed monthly fee, so entity setup doesn't sit disconnected from everything that follows.

- Bookkeeping calibrated to your new entity type from day one
- Payroll structured correctly for S-corp or partnership distributions
- Tax planning that reflects your entity choice, not last year's assumptions
- Real-time access through a secure online platform, so you and your CPA see the same numbers
- A natural path forward into [accounting system setup](/services/accounting-system-setup) once the structure is in place

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-left | image: westport-cpa-team-meeting.jpg | alt: "CPA team members discussing a client file together in a Westport office" | query: "accounting team discussion office meeting" -->
## Why Westport and Fairfield County businesses trust Abramson & Company

Ray founded Abramson & Company in 2005, and the firm has spent two decades working with business owners across Westport, Fairfield County, and the tri-state area of Connecticut, New York, and New Jersey. Clients in California's Bay Area work with the firm too, often needing guidance on how their state's rules interact with a Connecticut-based structure. That geographic range shows up in the questions the team knows to ask.

The firm is built so more than one person knows your file. If your regular contact is unavailable, another team member can pick up the conversation without making you start over. Inventory, cost of goods sold, and multi-location sales require a setup that separates margin from overhead from day one. See our [retail](/industries/retail) approach.

### Equine
icon: HeartPulse

Boarding fees, vet bills, feed costs, and breeding income each need their own line so you know what's actually profitable.

### Influencers
icon: Sparkles

## Collaborate in real time on our secure platform

Most accounting setups happen behind closed doors: you hand over your bank statements and wait for a finished product. We work differently.

Abramson & Company's secure online platform lets you watch your setup take shape in real time. Log in, see the chart of accounts as it's built, flag a category that doesn't fit, and get an answer the same day instead of waiting on a follow-up call. Your CPA team sees the same screen you do. That kind of visibility matters most in the first few weeks, when small corrections are easy to make and expensive to fix later.

That's been built into how the firm has worked since 2005, and it matters more during setup than at almost any other point in the relationship, because early decisions shape everything that follows.

### Retirement plan analysis
URL: /services/retirement-plan-analysis

<!-- block: intro-text | variant: centered -->
## Get a clear picture of your retirement readiness

Scattered 401(k) balances from old jobs. A SEP IRA you opened years ago and haven't looked at since. A vague sense that retirement is "handled," but no real proof of it. That's the situation many business owners and professionals in Westport bring to us, and it's exactly what a retirement plan analysis is built to fix.

A CPA-led review pulls every account into one picture: what you have, what it's costing you in taxes, and whether it lines up with the retirement you actually want. Abramson & Company has guided Fairfield County clients through this process since founding the firm in 2005, using the same plain-spoken approach behind our [tax and business advisory work](/services/tax). No jargon, no sales pitch, just a clear read on where you stand.

<!-- block: service-cards | variant: 3-col -->
## Who benefits from a retirement plan review

Retirement planning looks different depending on how you earn your income. Here's who tends to gain the most from a formal review.

### Small Business Owners
icon: Building2

Running payroll, covering overhead, and reinvesting in growth often push retirement contributions to the back burner. A review shows how much you can defer tax-free without straining cash flow, and whether a SEP IRA or Solo 401(k) fits your staffing situation better.

### Self-Employed Professionals
icon: Briefcase

Freelancers and solo practitioners have some of the widest contribution limits available, and some of the least guidance on how to use them. We map out contribution ceilings against your actual income so you're not guessing at deadlines or leaving deductions on the table.

### Real Estate Investors
icon: Home

Rental income, depreciation, and 1031 exchanges complicate what a "normal" retirement contribution looks like. A review accounts for your full income picture, not just W-2 wages. Many of our [real estate clients](/industries/real-estate) combine this analysis with broader tax planning.

### Professional Service Providers
icon: Scale

Attorneys, consultants, and other practice owners often have retirement accounts opened at different life stages with no coordination between them. We flag where fees, redundancy, or missed contribution room are quietly costing you. [Professional service providers](/industries/professional-service-providers) we work with often pair this with ongoing tax strategy.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: retirement-plan-review-checklist.jpg | alt: "Advisor and client reviewing retirement account statements together at a desk" | query: "advisor client reviewing financial documents desk" -->
## What our retirement plan analysis covers

A retirement plan analysis starts with the accounts you already have, not a blank slate. We gather statements from your 401(k), SEP IRA, Solo 401(k), or pension plan and evaluate them against your income, tax bracket, and timeline.

The review typically includes:

- A full inventory of existing retirement accounts and their current allocations
- An assessment of how much you're contributing versus how much you're allowed to contribute tax-free
- A comparison of your current plan structure against other tax-advantaged options
- A look at how retirement contributions interact with your [business entity type](/services/entity-type-analysis) and overall tax strategy
- Alignment between your retirement plan and any estate planning documents already in place
- A written summary of findings and recommended next steps, in language you can actually use

Nothing here is generic. Recommendations come from someone who already knows your tax return, your business structure, and your goals, because the same CPA team handles all three.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: business-owner-retirement-options.jpg | alt: "Small business owner discussing SEP IRA and Solo 401k options with advisor" | query: "small business owner financial advisor meeting" -->
## Retirement plan options for business owners and the self-employed

Choosing between a SEP IRA and a Solo 401(k) isn't a coin flip. It depends on your income level, whether you have employees, and how aggressively you want to contribute in a given year.

A SEP IRA is simple to set up and works well for business owners with fluctuating income or a small number of employees. A Solo 401(k) often allows higher total contributions and adds a Roth option that a SEP IRA doesn't offer. For business owners with staff beyond themselves, a SIMPLE IRA or small 401(k) plan may fit better, something we often map out alongside [business foundation services](/services/business-foundation-services/).

Abramson & Company walks through the math with you, comparing contribution limits, administrative cost, and tax impact side by side, so the plan you choose fits your business today, not a generic recommendation pulled from a brochure.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-left | image: cpa-team-collaboration-platform.jpg | alt: "CPA team members collaborating on a client retirement plan using a laptop" | query: "accounting team collaboration laptop office" -->
## How your CPA team supports your retirement strategy

Retirement decisions rarely happen in isolation. They connect to your tax return, your entity structure, and sometimes your exit plan for the business itself. That's why the same team handling your bookkeeping, payroll, or tax filing is the one reviewing your retirement accounts, not a separate advisor working from a different set of numbers.

Abramson & Company runs on a team-oriented model: multiple people on staff know your file well enough to step in when needed, so a question doesn't sit in an inbox waiting for one specific person to return. Documents and statements move through a secure online platform, so you can share information and see progress without a string of email attachments.

<!-- block: content-prose -->
## Serving Westport and the tri-state area

Abramson & Company is based in Westport, CT, and works with clients throughout Fairfield County and the greater CT-NY-NJ tri-state area. A number of clients are based farther out, including a concentration in California's Bay Area, connecting by phone and through the secure client platform rather than in-person meetings.

Wherever you're located, the retirement plan analysis works the same way: real numbers, reviewed by a CPA who already understands your tax situation.

<!-- block: cta-banner | variant: image-bg | image: schedule-retirement-consultation.jpg | alt: "Client and CPA advisor shaking hands after a retirement planning consultation" | query: "handshake advisor client office meeting" -->
## Schedule your retirement plan review

If your retirement accounts feel scattered, or no one has actually looked at all of them together, that's the gap this service closes. Bring whatever statements you have, even if it's just a login you haven't checked in a year. [Schedule a consultation](/contact) and we'll take it from there.

## Running your business shouldn't mean running yourself ragged

You started your business to build something, not to spend nights reconciling spreadsheets or double-checking whether last quarter's payroll filings went through correctly. Most owners we talk with in Westport and across Fairfield County aren't short on information. Between apps, articles, and well-meaning advice from other owners, there's plenty of that. What's missing is someone who knows their business well enough to say what actually matters.

That's the gap our business management services close. Instead of juggling separate contacts for bookkeeping, payroll, tax, and strategy, you get one CPA-led team that ties those pieces together into a single, coherent picture. This isn't facility oversight or property management. It's financial and operational guidance built around how your business actually runs.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: business-management-services-overview.jpg | alt: "Accountant organizing financial reports and documents for a small business" | query: "accountant organizing financial documents office" -->
## What business management services include at Abramson

Business management services at Abramson & Company cover the financial and operational oversight small-to-midsize businesses need day to day, not the maintenance, leasing, or tenant work a property manager handles. Think of it as a standing seat at the table for your company's numbers and decisions.

Here's what that looks like in practice:

- Cash flow monitoring and forecasting, so you know what's coming before it hits your account
- Monthly and quarterly [financial reporting](/services/outsourced-accounting) built for decisions, not just compliance
- Vendor and [payroll](/services/payroll) coordination handled by people who already know your business
- Budget and expense oversight tied to your actual goals, not generic industry benchmarks
- Strategic decision support when you're weighing a hire, a lease, or a new line of business
- Coordination across [bookkeeping](/services/bookkeeping), payroll, [tax](/services/tax), and advisory so nothing falls through the cracks between services

Each piece runs through the same team and the same fixed monthly fee, so the picture stays whole instead of scattered across separate vendors and separate invoices.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: business-management-team-meeting.jpg | alt: "CPA team reviewing client financial reports together at a conference table" | query: "accounting team collaborating office meeting" -->
## One team that knows your business from every angle

Business management pricing at Abramson works on a bundled, fixed monthly fee. You know the cost upfront, and it covers the coordination between bookkeeping, payroll, tax, and advisory work rather than a separate invoice for every phone call or question.

More importantly, more than one person on our team knows your business well enough to actually answer your questions. If your usual contact is out, someone else can pick up the conversation without making you start over. That's a deliberate part of how Ray built the firm: a team-oriented culture where the knowledge about your business doesn't sit in one person's inbox.

For a business owner, that means fewer dropped threads and less time spent re-explaining your own company to whoever happens to answer the phone.

Different industries carry different operational headaches. Here's where our business management clients typically need the most support.

### Real Estate
icon: Building2

Multi-entity structures, property-level P&Ls, and 1031 timelines mean [real estate](/industries/real-estate) clients need reporting that rolls up cleanly across properties and partnerships. We track cash flow by entity so you can see which properties are actually performing.

### Professional Service Providers
icon: Briefcase

[Law firms, consultancies, and agencies](/industries/professional-service-providers) deal with uneven billing cycles and partner draws that complicate cash flow planning. We coordinate payroll, partner distributions, and tax planning so cash on hand matches what's actually owed.

### Retail
icon: Receipt

Inventory financing, seasonal swings, and thin margins mean [retail](/industries/retail) businesses need close, current numbers, not a report that shows up six weeks late. We keep clients current on cost of goods, inventory turns, and vendor terms.

### Equine Businesses
icon: HeartPulse

Boarding income, vet and farrier bills, and seasonal show expenses create cash flow patterns that don't look like a typical small business. We build reporting around those rhythms instead of forcing a generic template onto an equine operation.

### Influencers and Content Creators
icon: Sparkles

Brand deal income, platform payouts, and self-employment tax obligations arrive unevenly and from multiple sources. We help track income by channel and plan tax payments so a good month doesn't turn into a tax-time surprise.

## Current openings in accounting, tax, and payroll

icon: FileCheck

This role assists with not-for-profit and small business audit engagements, testing internal controls and preparing supporting documentation under a senior accountant's direction. Prior audit exposure through coursework or internship is a plus.

### Payroll Specialist

Process multi-client payroll runs, manage tax filings and compliance deadlines, and answer client questions about withholdings and benefits. Attention to detail matters more than years of experience.

### Senior Tax Accountant

Students pursuing an accounting degree gain hands-on exposure to bookkeeping, tax season workflow, and client communication, with mentorship from CPAs who remember being interns themselves.

## Resources

### Long-Term Care: How You Can Financially Prepare for the Expense
URL: /resources/long-term-care-how-you-can-financially-prepare-for-the-expen

Nobody plans for long-term care the way they plan for a mortgage or a child's college fund, and that's exactly the problem. By the time a parent needs help bathing, dressing, or managing medication, the family is usually making decisions under pressure, often paying retail rates for care that could have been funded years earlier at a fraction of the stress. Long-term care is not a medical emergency you insure against after the fact. It's a financial risk you manage in advance, the same way you'd manage liability exposure or a concentrated stock position. For families in Westport and across Fairfield County, where home health aide rates run higher than the national average, the earlier this conversation happens, the more options stay on the table.

This post walks through what long-term care actually costs, how insurance stacks up against self-funding, where the VA Aid and Attendance benefit fits for veterans and surviving spouses, and how to build a funding plan that blends all three instead of betting everything on one.

## What long-term care actually costs

Most people underestimate this by a wide margin. National data consistently shows a private room in a nursing home running well over $100,000 a year, with assisted living facilities averaging somewhere in the $60,000 to $70,000 range annually, and a full-time home health aide often costing $75,000 or more a year depending on hours and skill level. In Fairfield County, home care and facility rates typically run above these national figures because of local wage costs and demand.

Here's the number that catches most families off guard: average care duration. Someone who needs long-term care doesn't need it for six months. Multi-year stays are common, and dementia-related care frequently extends five years or longer. Multiply even a conservative $85,000 annual cost by three or four years, and you're looking at a $250,000 to $350,000 expense that most retirement plans never explicitly budgeted for.

## Long-term care insurance vs self-funding

There are really three ways to pay for long-term care: a dedicated insurance policy, savings and investments earmarked for the purpose, or a hybrid that uses both. Each has real tradeoffs, and the right answer depends on age, health, family history, and the size of the estate being protected.

| Factor | Long-term care insurance | Self-funding from savings |
|---|---|---|
| Best time to start | Age 50-65, while still insurable | Any age, but needs decades to build |
| Predictability | Fixed premium, defined benefit | Depends on market performance and timing |
| Underwriting risk | Denied or priced high if health declines | No underwriting required |
| Estate impact | Preserves other assets for heirs | Directly depletes savings or investments |
| Flexibility | Benefits tied to policy terms | Full control over how funds are spent |
| Inflation protection | Available as a rider, at added cost | Depends on investment growth outpacing costs |

Insurance makes the most sense for people in their mid-50s to mid-60s who are still healthy enough to qualify and who want to protect a specific pool of assets, such as a business or a home they intend to pass down. Premiums have risen sharply over the past decade, so getting quotes earlier rather than later matters more than it used to.

Self-funding works best for households with substantial investment portfolios who can absorb a six-figure care expense without derailing retirement income. It requires discipline: the money has to actually be earmarked, not folded into a general investment account and hoped for later. If your portfolio strategy hasn't been stress-tested against a scenario like this, it's worth revisiting how your [balanced investment portfolio](/resources/strategically-balancing-your-investment-portfolio-why-set-it) is positioned for a large, unplanned withdrawal a decade or two out.

Most of our clients land on a hybrid: a smaller insurance policy or hybrid life/LTC product to cover a base level of risk, paired with dedicated savings to cover the gap. This spreads the risk instead of concentrating it in one strategy that might not hold up.

## The VA benefit veterans and surviving spouses often miss

For veterans and their surviving spouses, there's a funding source that gets overlooked constantly: the [VA Aid and Attendance and Housebound benefit](https://www.va.gov/pension/aid-attendance-housebound/). This is an increased monthly pension amount available to eligible wartime veterans, and their surviving spouses, who need help with daily activities like bathing, dressing, or managing medications, or who are housebound.

The eligibility rules involve wartime service dates, income limits net of unreimbursed medical expenses, and net worth thresholds, so this isn't a benefit you self-diagnose from a web search. But for a veteran family already facing $70,000-plus in annual home care costs, an additional benefit in the range of several hundred to over $2,000 a month, depending on marital status and disability level, changes the funding math meaningfully. If there's a veteran or a surviving spouse anywhere in the family tree who might need care in the next five to ten years, it's worth checking eligibility now, before the need is urgent and the application is being rushed.

## Building a funding plan that blends all three

A long-term care funding strategy that actually holds up usually layers three pieces together instead of leaning on one:

1. **A baseline insurance or hybrid policy** purchased while still insurable, sized to cover a meaningful chunk of the projected annual cost rather than all of it.
2. **A dedicated savings or investment bucket**, separate from retirement income accounts, built specifically to cover the gap between insurance benefits and actual costs.
3. **Benefit eligibility review**, including VA Aid and Attendance for veteran households, checked and documented well before care is needed.

The order matters. Insurance underwriting gets harder and more expensive with age and health changes, so that decision should happen first, ideally in your 50s or early 60s. Savings targets can then be calculated as the gap between what insurance will pay and what care will actually cost in your area. Benefit eligibility should be confirmed on paper, not assumed, because income and net worth limits shift and documentation requirements are specific.

This is also where the estate and tax picture connects. Some long-term care expenses and a portion of qualified long-term care insurance premiums are deductible as medical expenses if they exceed the applicable threshold of adjusted gross income, as outlined in [IRS Publication 502](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p502). That deduction won't fund the whole plan, but for households already itemizing, it's real money that shouldn't be left on the table. Coordinating this with your broader tax strategy, the same way you would with any major deduction, is part of why long-term care planning belongs in the same conversation as your annual [tax planning](/resources/maximizing-your-tax-refund-a-strategic-guide-to-tax-planning) rather than treated as a separate, standalone decision.

## How to start without feeling overwhelmed

Start with three numbers: your current age, your family health history, and a rough estimate of investable assets outside your primary residence. Those three data points determine whether insurance, self-funding, or a blend makes sense, and whether VA benefits apply to anyone in the household. From there, a real plan involves an insurance quote comparison, a savings target tied to actual local care costs, and a benefits eligibility check, not a single decision made in a single afternoon.

This is also a good moment to look at your overall financial picture rather than long-term care in isolation. If retirement income, insurance coverage, and investment allocation haven't been reviewed together recently, a broader [financial planning](/resources/5-tips-to-build-a-healthy-money-mindset-and-grow-your-finances) conversation often surfaces gaps that a long-term care discussion alone would miss.

## Common Questions

**How much does long-term care typically cost per year?**
National estimates put a private nursing home room well above $100,000 a year, assisted living in the $60,000-$70,000 range, and a full-time home health aide around $75,000 or more annually. Costs in Fairfield County typically run higher than these national figures due to local wage and demand levels.

**Is long-term care insurance worth it if I'm already in my 60s?**
It depends on health status and how much of your estate you're trying to protect. Premiums rise with age and underwriting gets stricter, so it's worth getting quotes now rather than waiting, but a hybrid life/LTC product or a self-funding strategy may make more sense if health issues have already surfaced.

**Can veterans get help paying for long-term care?**
Eligible wartime veterans and surviving spouses may qualify for the VA Aid and Attendance and Housebound benefit, an increased pension amount for those needing help with daily activities. Eligibility depends on service dates, income net of medical expenses, and net worth, detailed at [va.gov](https://www.va.gov/pension/aid-attendance-housebound/).

**Are long-term care expenses tax deductible?**
Some long-term care costs and qualified insurance premiums count as deductible medical expenses once they exceed the applicable percentage of adjusted gross income, per [IRS Publication 502](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p502). Whether this helps depends on your total itemized deductions for the year.

Long-term care is one of the biggest unbudgeted expenses a family will face, and the funding decisions work best when they're made years before they're needed. If you want help building a plan that blends insurance, savings, and any available benefits into one coordinated strategy, [contact our team](/contact) to talk through your specific situation.
